discovery: Rydberg blockade and programmable Rydberg atom arrays for quantum simulation and computation

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: The nominees turned the strong, long-range interaction between Rydberg atoms into a controllable quantum resource. Lukin co-proposed the dipole blockade mechanism for neutral-atom quantum gates (2000-2001). In 2009 Saffman and Browaeys independently gave the first direct observations of Rydberg blockade between two individually trapped atoms, and Saffman demonstrated the first neutral-atom CNOT gate. Browaeys and Lukin then built programmable arrays of hundreds of optical-tweezer-trapped atoms, assembled defect-free atom by atom. With these arrays they observed quantum magnetism, ordered phases and quantum phase transitions, quantum many-body scars and topological spin liquids. Lukin's group went on to run algorithms on error-corrected logical qubits. The result is a new platform, built from first principles of atomic physics, that now bridges condensed-matter physics, quantum information and technology, and has defined an entire field.
